atomic_red_team_reference.atomic_name: Windows Command Shell tests using batch files and file output

primary_mitre.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell

candidate_wazuh_rule.description: Executable file dropped in folder commonly used by malware

executed_behaviors: The launcher creates a run-specific command file under the current user's LocalAppData Temp directory.
cmd.exe executes the run-specific command file.
The command file writes a run-specific result file under ProgramData.
findstr.exe queries the run identifier in the result file.
process_chain: trigger.bat -> powershell.exe -> cmd.exe -> run-specific command file
expected_artifacts: Result query stdout and stderr files
explicit_non_actions: The command file does not download, decode or launch an external payload.
No network, persistence, credential, account or security-control operation is performed.
No unrelated Temp or ProgramData content is removed.

negative_behavior_catalog.behavior: The command file does not download content from a network location.
The command file does not decode or launch an external payload.
No credential or account operation is performed.

causal_boundaries: File creation is separate from later cmd.exe execution.
The result file confirms the command file ran; the FileCreate alert alone does not prove execution.
The later findstr.exe process is a query and is not part of the command file action.
Unrelated PowerShell policy-test files in Temp are not the current RUN anchor.
preferred_anchor: A current-RUN wazuh-alerts-* event for rule 92213 whose targetFilename is the run-specific Temp command file.
correlation_requirements: The alert targetFilename must contain the current RUN ID.
Archives must link the creating PowerShell, the cmd.exe process and the result file.
known_telemetry_gaps: The active rule maps Temp executable-file creation to T1105, but a local file creation alert alone does not prove network ingress.
FileCreate and process execution are separate events and must not be collapsed into one behavior.
